title: Iraq’s World Cup dream gets boost as travel plans drawn up for players to leave Middle East
content:
The Iraq men’s soccer team have drawn up new travel plans for their crucial World Cup qualifying play-off, easing concerns they will be unable to compete in Mexico at the end of this month.

Iraq are due to face either Bolivia or Suriname in Monterey on March 31, with the winner progressing to the World Cup finals this summer, but their preparations have faced huge challenges since war broke out in neighbouring Iran last month.

Sources briefed on the deal say talks have since been held with FIFA and a new plan has been devised for Iraq’s players to journey to the Jordanian capital of Amman next Friday, where they will be able to start an onward journey to Mexico 11 days out from their one-off game at the Estadio BBVA.

Airspace over Iraq remains closed to all commercial flights amid continued bombing in the region, prompting Iraq head coach Graham Arnold to cast doubt over their involvement in FIFA’s six-team play-off tournament.

Arnold had suggested it would likely require a 25-hour journey by road for his Iraq-based players to reach Istanbul, Turkey before then boarding a long-haul flight to Mexico.

That would mean an estimated 60 per cent of Iraq’s squad would be facing a gruelling journey and the complex logistics prompted Arnold to ask for Iraq’s crucial fixture to be postponed during an interview with CNN.

The doubts over Iraq’s participation have run alongside the uncertainty that continues to hang over Iran’s involvement in this summer’s World Cup finals.

The ongoing American-Israeli operations against Iran, which began on February 27, saw the Iranian sports minster suggest his country should not take their place at the tournament earlier this week. U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday it would not be “appropriate” for Iran to feature for “their own life and safety”, only for the Iran soccer team to later post on Instagram that “no one” can exclude them from the World Cup.

Trump’s message, posted on his Truth Social platform, went against an earlier Instagram post from FIFA boss Gianni Infantino, who said the president had reiterated that Iran would be “welcome” in the U.S. this summer.

FIFA has given no indication that Iran will not be able to feature at the World Cup but Iraq would be among the leading candidates as a replacement if another nation from the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) was the preferred option. Iraq beat UAE in the fifth round of AFC qualifying to win a place in the inter-confederation play-offs.

Iraq last qualified for a World Cup finals 40 years ago.
